subject.title: Bug: Gateway falsely marks healthy local vLLM endpoints as timed out/overloaded, causing 1–23 min fallback cascades

question: Is the current shipped set of adjacent fallback, timeout, and gateway-startup fixes enough to close this broad local vLLM cascade report, or should this remain the canonical live-repro item until a current-main vLLM trace proves the remaining symptoms gone?
rationale: The code and related PR history prove multiple slices were fixed, but the original report described a combined local vLLM plus gateway RPC cascade that has not been replayed on current main.

options.title: Keep as live-repro canonical
options.body: Leave this issue open until a maintainer captures or reviews a current-main local vLLM trace covering provider timing, fallback decisions, and gateway RPC latency.

options.title: Split the remaining symptom
options.body: Open a narrower follow-up for only the healthy-vLLM false-timeout or gateway-RPC latency path and close this once that canonical follow-up is linked.

options.title: Close from external proof
options.body: Close as implemented only if maintainers already have out-of-band current-main/live-release evidence that the original cascade no longer reproduces.

recommendation.title: Keep as live-repro canonical
recommendation.body: Leave this issue open until a maintainer captures or reviews a current-main local vLLM trace covering provider timing, fallback decisions, and gateway RPC latency.

likelyOwner.reason: The issue is assigned to osolmaz and the adjacent cron fallback/preflight fix history makes this the best available owner for deciding proof sufficiency.
